breaking_news.headline: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady and hints at rate hike later this year
breaking_news.summary: The Federal Reserve left its benchmark interest rates unchanged Wednesday, and signaled its next move could be a rate increase. It's the first rate decision under the new Fed chairman, Kevin Warsh.

breaking_news.headline: With Iran deal, Trump told ships to 'start your engines.' That's not happening yet
breaking_news.summary: Iran's control of the Strait of Hormuz inflicted global pain during the months-long conflict with the U.S. and Israel. A tentative deal is in place, but questions remain about the key waterway.

breaking_news.headline: Here's how much the Iran war cost -- and how its effects will linger
breaking_news.summary: More than three months after the U.S. and Israel launched their war on Iran, the costs and aftereffects are felt around the world.

breaking_news.headline: Poll: Most Americans have the summer blues about Trump and the economy
breaking_news.summary: A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll finds a record low share of Americans approve of President Trump's job performance and his handling of the economy heading into the summer before a key midterm election.

breaking_news.headline: Here is how SpaceX could turn up in your current investments
breaking_news.summary: SpaceX stock hit the market last week. Here's how it could turn up in your retirement or investment portfolio.

breaking_news.headline: Alan Greenspan, the legendary former Federal Reserve chair, dies
breaking_news.summary: During his chairmanship, Greenspan was celebrated as possibly the best central banker in history. But later, his reputation was tarnished by the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

breaking_news.headline: Did you know? Alan Greenspan and Ayn Rand were close friends
breaking_news.summary: One of the most intellectually important relationships in the life of the late Fed chair Alan Greenspan was with his close friend, the formidable novelist and libertarian thinker Ayn Rand.

breaking_news.headline: When falling housing prices are good news — and when they're not
breaking_news.summary: Denver renters are celebrating falling housing costs. But sometimes cheaper housing is a sign of economic decline. How can you tell the difference?

breaking_news.headline: Trump anticipates better relationship with Colombia under new leader
breaking_news.summary: Abelardo de la Espriella, who preliminary results suggest is Colombia's next president, had Trump's endorsement.

breaking_news.headline: Irish government to contribute £197m to cross-border rail services
breaking_news.summary: The money will come from the last allocation from the Irish government's Shared Island Fund.

breaking_news.headline: Spider which uses spring trap to capture prey discovered in Australia
breaking_news.summary: Researchers say their hunting method - which allows them to prey on dangerous ants - is unprecedented.

breaking_news.headline: Zambia ex-president's family wins latest legal battle over what should happen to his body
breaking_news.summary: Edgar Lungu's family and the Zambian government remain in dispute 12 months after he died.

breaking_news.headline: UN commission of inquiry says Israel committing genocide in Gaza by deliberately targeting children
breaking_news.summary: Israel rejects the new report by the three-member expert panel, calling it a "libellous sham".

breaking_news.headline: Iran says no new commitments on nuclear sites after Vance says inspectors to be invited back
breaking_news.summary: Iran's foreign ministry says it made "no new commitments" on nuclear inspections after talks in Switzerland.

breaking_news.headline: Dozens of ships head through Strait of Hormuz after US-Iran deal
breaking_news.summary: Traffic in the waterway has risen since the US and Iran signed a deal aimed at ending the war, including 42 ships on Saturday alone.

breaking_news.headline: Drowning deaths soar in France as Europe buckles in peak of heatwave
breaking_news.summary: Forty people have drowned in heatwave-related deaths in France since last Thursday, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu says.

breaking_news.headline: Tesla crash that killed a woman under US federal investigation
breaking_news.summary: A Tesla driver on Friday said he was using ‘self-driving’ technology after his vehicle sped into a Texas home.

breaking_news.headline: Millions in UK could claim share of £3bn after Apple case given green light
breaking_news.summary: Apple rejected the suggestion its practices are anti-competitive, saying many customers rely on third-party alternatives.

breaking_news.headline: Tech giant Oracle cuts 21,000 jobs as it embraces AI
breaking_news.summary: The cuts are part of a wider trend among tech firms as they spend hundreds of billions of dollars on AI.

breaking_news.headline: Do you know your 'sweat score'? The rise of hydration tech
breaking_news.summary: Hydration tracking gadgets are flooding the market but is it too much information?
